text:
For a unit vector in the \(x\)-\(z\) plane, take

\[
\vec n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta).
\]

Thus,

\[
P_{\vec n}=\vec n\cdot\vec P
=\frac{\hbar}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Let its \(+\hbar/2\) eigenvector be \(\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}\). The eigenvalue equation gives

\[
(\cos\theta-1)a+\sin\theta\,b=0,
\]

so

\[
\frac{b}{a}
=\frac{1-\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}
=\tan\frac{\theta}{2}.
\]

Normalization \( |a|^2+|b|^2=1\) therefore yields

\[
\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos(\theta/2)\\[2mm]
\sin(\theta/2)
\end{pmatrix},
\]

up to an arbitrary overall phase. The factor \(\hbar\) belongs to the eigenvalue, not the normalized eigenvector.

Answer: B
